newsitem.title: USA: Palm Beach Cty, Fla., bonds in technical default.
newsitem.headline: Palm Beach Cty, Fla., bonds in technical default.

text.p: Some $288.5 million of Palm Beach County, Fla., bonds that financed two biomass cogeneration plants are in technical default because the partnership that owns the plants filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, the bond counsel for the issues said Friday.
"They're not in payment default," bond counsel Rick Miller said. "But an event of bankruptcy is a default under the bond documents."
The bonds in question are three series of Palm Beach County Industrial Development Revenue Bonds:
--Okeelanta Power Limited Partnership Project, Series 1993A, principal of $160 million.
--Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, tax-exempt Series 1994A, principal amount of $120.5 million.
--Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, taxable Series 1994 B, principal amount of $8,000,000.
SunTrust Bank recently succeeded the Bank of New York as trustee for the bonds. The change was made at bondholders' request, an official involved with the issue said.
Annual debt service on the bonds is about $10 million and the next payment is due June 1.
The bonds financed construction of two cogeneration plants owned by the Okeelanta Power and Gator Generating Company Limited Partnerships, which filed for Chapter 11 bankrutpcy on Wednesday.

The partnerships are owned by owned by Pacific Gas & Electric Co, a unit of PG&E Corp and Bechtel. They said the bankrtupcy filing was necessary because of a legal dispute with Florida Power & Light Co over FPL's obligation to buy power produced by the plants.
